Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (central names registry) and the competent Registro Mercantil Provincial for the registered office; deed authenticated by a Spanish notary.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): arts. 20-22 (escritura y constitución), arts. 23-28 (statutory contents, contributions and capital), arts. 9-11 (registered office), arts. 58-62 (administration), arts. 210-214 (appointment of administrators), arts. 132-138 (NIF and registration).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura pública de constitución of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (public incorporation deed), filed with the Mercantile Registry.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 48 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and paid up before execution of the deed, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate issued by a Spanish credit institution. Non-cash contributions must be valued by an independent expert and described in the deed. The bank funds remain segregated until the NIF is obtained and the company is registered; after registration, the administrators may release them.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certificate issued by the regional fire brigade in accordance with Código Técnico de la Edificación (CTE) DB-SI/DB-SI, including emergency lighting, extinguishers and evacuation routes; structural load inspection certificate for the building's actual floor loads from cleanroom/robotics equipment; municipal occupancy licence; occupational health and safety evaluation by an accredited mutua, including cleanroom ISO 14644 classification and machine safety compliance with RD 1215/1997 and RD 1644/2002.

Paid-in capital rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and paid up before execution of the deed, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate issued by a Spanish credit institution. Non-cash contributions must be valued by an independent expert and described in the deed. The bank funds remain segregated until the NIF is obtained and the company is registered; after registration, the administrators may release them.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including its Sede Electrónica portal. The AEAT administers Spanish tax identification, Value Added Tax, Corporate Income Tax, customs and related registration obligations.

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) through the AEAT. The incorporation deed and registration details are submitted using Modelo 036, normally initially for a provisional NIF and subsequently for the definitive NIF after registration in the Commercial Registry. The filing must identify the registered office, tax domicile, economic activities, directors, beneficial ownership information where required, and tax representative or attorney-in-fact. A foreign shareholder or foreign corporate director must provide the relevant foreign tax identification details and, where required, obtain a Spanish Número de Identidad de Extranjero (NIE) or NIF. Foreign corporate documents generally require legalization or apostille and an official Spanish translation unless an applicable treaty or EU documentation rule provides otherwise. The Spanish NIF is also used as the domestic VAT identification number; intra-Community VAT transactions require validation of the number in the VIES system and, where applicable, registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios through Modelo 036.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) through the AEAT. The incorporation deed and registration details are submitted using Modelo 036, normally initially for a provisional NIF and subsequently for the definitive NIF after registration in the Commercial Registry. The filing must identify the registered office, tax domicile, economic activities, directors, beneficial ownership information where required, and tax representative or attorney-in-fact. A foreign shareholder or foreign corporate director must provide the relevant foreign tax identification details and, where required, obtain a Spanish Número de Identidad de Extranjero (NIE) or NIF. Foreign corporate documents generally require legalization or apostille and an official Spanish translation unless an applicable treaty or EU documentation rule provides otherwise. The Spanish NIF is also used as the domestic VAT identification number; intra-Community VAT transactions require validation of the number in the VIES system and, where applicable, registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios through Modelo 036.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

Spain has no general United States-style check-the-box election for an SL. The SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal entity, with worldwide taxation if Spanish tax resident. Available elections or special regimes may include Spanish tax consolidation, the special regime for mergers and other qualifying restructurings, the Canary Islands tax regime where applicable, and other sector-specific regimes subject to statutory conditions and formal elections. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions, impose inclusion adjustments or restrict relief for arrangements producing deduction-without-inclusion, double deduction or equivalent mismatches. The entity cannot generally elect transparent pass-through treatment merely by filing a classification election.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

None; Spain has no general domestic turnover threshold below which an ordinary business may remain outside VAT registration. A person carrying on an economic activity must generally register and comply with VAT obligations from the commencement of the activity. Separate thresholds and conditions can apply to specific EU small-business, distance-selling and intra-Community regimes.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Goods exported from Spain to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT where the Spanish supplier or an authorized customer transports or dispatches the goods and the export is evidenced by customs records and proof of exit from the EU customs territory. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are dispatched to that Member State, the supplier satisfies invoicing and EC Sales List reporting requirements, and transport and customer-status evidence are retained. Services may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT or exempt under the place-of-supply rules where supplied to a non-Spanish business customer or otherwise meet the statutory conditions; the result depends on the service category, customer status, place of use and enjoyment, and any applicable special rule. Export zero-rating is not available solely because the customer is non-resident; documentary proof and the applicable place-of-supply or export conditions must be satisfied.

  • Spanish export customs declaration, normally the electronic DUA export declaration and its MRN
  • Customs confirmation or electronic evidence that the goods exited the European Union customs territory
  • Commercial invoice, packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR or equivalent
  • Purchase order, sales contract and proof linking the exported goods to the Spanish supplier and invoice
  • Customer VAT identification and intra-Community supply evidence where the transaction is an intra-Community supply rather than an extra-EU export
  • Proof of payment or foreign inward remittance where commercially or audit-relevant; Spain does not generally require an inward remittance certificate as a universal VAT zero-rating document

Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance system for all taxpayers. Electronic invoicing is mandatory in specified public-sector transactions and is being extended to qualifying private B2B transactions under Law 18/2022, subject to implementing regulations and statutory transition periods. The Immediate Supply of Information system (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including entities with turnover exceeding the statutory threshold, VAT groups and REDEME participants, to transmit prescribed invoice-register data electronically to the AEAT within the applicable deadlines. The Veri*Factu and certified billing-system rules require compliant billing software, integrity and traceability controls, and prescribed transmission or availability features for affected taxpayers under the applicable implementation timetable. There is no general requirement for an AEAT digital stamp or pre-clearance of every invoice. Invoices must contain the statutory data, including issuer and customer identification, VAT number where required, date, sequential number, taxable base, rate, VAT amount and applicable exemption or reverse-charge reference.

Spain has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for qualifying export VAT treatment. Export proceeds may remain abroad subject to applicable banking, anti-money-laundering, accounting and foreign-investment reporting rules. If export or intra-Community conditions are not proven, the AEAT may deny the exemption, assess output VAT, recover improperly refunded or deducted input VAT, and charge late-payment interest. Administrative tax penalties depend on the infringement and may generally range from 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid or refunded tax, with aggravation or reduction rules. False, incomplete or manipulated customs evidence may also trigger customs sanctions, repayment of customs or VAT benefits and related interest. Deliberate tax fraud can create criminal exposure where the statutory tax-loss thresholds and other elements of a tax offense are met.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain applies full euro convertibility under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union; no exchange-control authorization is required for current or capital transactions. Dividend and profit remittances from a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada to non-resident shareholders are freely permitted, subject only to corporate income tax filings, transfer-pricing documentation, anti-money-laundering compliance, and mandatory balance-of-payments declarations to the Banco de España where thresholds exceed EUR 50,000 per transaction.

Export proceeds surrender rules

There is no Spanish statutory export-proceeds surrender rule or mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may keep receivables in foreign currency or convert to euro at market rates. Amounts paid or collected from non-residents must be reported to the Banco de España through the official 'Declaración de Transacciones con el Exterior' within the applicable calendar-based statistical deadlines (normally the first twenty days of the month following the transaction for large flows).

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks, the Single Supervisory Mechanism of the European Central Bank, and the Spanish Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation for foreign-exchange statistical supervision.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Revolut Fit: High

Feasibility rating: Medium-High. Spanish-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) under PSD2, including Revolut Business, N26 Business, and Bnext, can provide EUR IBANs, segregated funds, and low-fee FX conversion, and are supervised by the Banco de España. However, they generally cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit, do not offer documentary collections, and are not direct members of TARGET2/SWIFT; they are suitable as a secondary liquidity rail but not as the primary account for ISIC 3250 trade settlements.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

UBO registered in a high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction, or ownership chain containing bearer share structures

Root cause: UBO registered in a high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction, or ownership chain containing bearer share structures

Defense evidence: Notarized Spanish escritura, certified register of final beneficiaries (Registro de Titularidad Real) issued not more than 3 months prior, organizational charts identifying all individuals with >25% control, passports/NIE of UBOs, sworn source-of-wealth declarations, and a risk assessment from a registered Spanish AML compliance officer.
Unusually large first inbound transfer for surgical laparoscopy tower production without evident underlying trade contract

Root cause: Unusually large first inbound transfer for surgical laparoscopy tower production without evident underlying trade contract

Defense evidence: Commercial agreements with purchase orders, ISIC 3250 manufacturing plant license, ISO 13485 and CE certificates, detailed proforma invoices, list of component suppliers, projected cash flow statement, and a letter of explanation describing the capital injection into the SL's escrow account.
Directors or counterparties flagged on PEP, sanctions, or adverse media screenings

Root cause: Directors or counterparties flagged on PEP, sanctions, or adverse media screenings

Defense evidence: EU Financial Sanctions consolidated list check results, national police certificate of criminal records (certificado de antecedentes penales), legalization and apostille of foreign documentation, favorable legal opinion on the non-application of restrictive measures, and bank-specific enhanced due diligence questionnaire with direct source-of-funds evidence (bank statements and sales ledger).

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant inbound equity inflows must be transferred via SWIFT/SEPA from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Spanish SL's named escrow or operational account in EUR, with the SWIFT field 70 narrative clearly stating 'Capital subscription' and referencing the notarial deed. The SL must classify the transaction under the Bank of Spain balance-of-payments code for direct investment equity (concept 340) and file the electronic declaration unless exempted; the capital increase must also be formalized before a notary and registered in the Registro Mercantil within the statutory period to avoid infraction penalties.Disbursements should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for direct supplier payments, TARGET2/SCT for intra-EU euro settlements, and via UCP 600-compliant commercial letters of credit issued by a Spanish trade-finance bank for Latin American and high-risk transactions. Documentary collections and purchase-order financing may be used in parallel, with each outbound transfer annotated using ISO 20022 purpose codes, e.g., 'TRAD' or 'CGDS', and underlying transport documents retained to prove genuine economic substance.Outright EUR/USD FX forwards concluded with authorized Spanish bank counterparties under ISDA 2002 master agreementsNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CLP, USD/MXN, and USD/BRL for Latin American revenues faced by the laparoscopy tower exporterCross-currency basis swaps for EUR/USD and EUR/LatAm currency pair exposuresEuropean-style vanilla FX options (call/put) purchased for negative-follow-up protection on awarded tendersCurrency swap agreements with non-financial counterparties solely for actual treasury risk hedging, subject to EMIR clearing exemptions

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: Medium-High. Spanish-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) under PSD2, including Revolut Business, N26 Business, and Bnext, can provide EUR IBANs, segregated funds, and low-fee FX conversion, and are supervised by the Banco de España. However, they generally cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit, do not offer documentary collections, and are not direct members of TARGET2/SWIFT; they are suitable as a secondary liquidity rail but not as the primary account for ISIC 3250 trade settlements.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% for outbound dividends paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident shareholder, applied under the Non-Resident Income Tax regime (IRNR). Spanish-resident corporate shareholders may qualify for the participation exemption if holding at least 5% for one year.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the close of the tax year. For a calendar-year fiscal year ending 31 December, the statutory deadline is 25 July; for non-calendar fiscal years, the same 25-day rule applies after the six-month anniversary of the fiscal year-end.

Deadline: · Frequency:

For calendar-year taxpayers, instalments are due within the first 20 calendar days of April, October and December. For a non-calendar fiscal year, the due date is the first 20 days after the relevant instalment period as scheduled in Article 40 LIS and annual AEAT regulations.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Block A / Identification Box Tax identification number (NIF), registered address, dominant economic activity code (CNAE/ISIC 3250), fiscal period, type of return (individual, consolidated, complementaria). A non-resident permanent establishment (PE) must use the Spanish NIF assigned to the PE, enter the PE's Spanish address and report the manufacturing activity under CNAE 3250; a non-resident without a Spanish PE must not submit Form 200. Late filing of Form 200 without prior AEAT assessment gives rise to an extemporaneous filing surcharge of 1% per month up to 15%, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75% per annum). A late return with no tax due attracts a fixed fine of EUR 200 to EUR 6,000. Incorrect or false returns trigger proportional penalties under Articles 191–193 LGT: from 50% to 150% of the under-assessed amount, plus interest and administrative costs.
Boxes 0031–0045 / Accounting Result and Tax Adjustments Report the statutory accounting profit or loss, then apply permanent and temporary adjustments to reconcile the accounting result with taxable income, including depreciation, provisions, amortisation, valuation adjustments and tax-exempt income. The PE must compute profits attributable to the Spanish activity in accordance with Article 13 of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law (LIS); internal chargebacks from the head office are deductible only if they meet arm's-length substance requirements and are adequately evidenced. Late filing of Form 200 without prior AEAT assessment gives rise to an extemporaneous filing surcharge of 1% per month up to 15%, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75% per annum). A late return with no tax due attracts a fixed fine of EUR 200 to EUR 6,000. Incorrect or false returns trigger proportional penalties under Articles 191–193 LGT: from 50% to 150% of the under-assessed amount, plus interest and administrative costs.
Box 0046–0052 / Tax Base, Loss Offsets and Incentives State the taxable base before and after offsetting carried-forward tax losses (BIN), available tax credits and incentives, and the reduced new-company rate where applicable. A non-resident PE may offset only those losses that are genuinely attributable to the PE; resident-only incentives such as certain regional credits are not available to non-resident entities. Late filing of Form 200 without prior AEAT assessment gives rise to an extemporaneous filing surcharge of 1% per month up to 15%, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75% per annum). A late return with no tax due attracts a fixed fine of EUR 200 to EUR 6,000. Incorrect or false returns trigger proportional penalties under Articles 191–193 LGT: from 50% to 150% of the under-assessed amount, plus interest and administrative costs.
Box 0054–0058 / Quota, Withholdings and Tax Credits Compute the total corporate tax at 25% or 15% reduced rate, deduct prepayments, withholding tax credits, double-tax relief and any refundable tax credit amounts. Non-resident PEs must not use resident-only credits and must reconcile Spain-source income with treaty provisions; excess credits require a tax treaty refund request or Form 210 procedure. Late filing of Form 200 without prior AEAT assessment gives rise to an extemporaneous filing surcharge of 1% per month up to 15%, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75% per annum). A late return with no tax due attracts a fixed fine of EUR 200 to EUR 6,000. Incorrect or false returns trigger proportional penalties under Articles 191–193 LGT: from 50% to 150% of the under-assessed amount, plus interest and administrative costs.
Box 0060–0064 / Result and Payment Final tax due or amount to be refunded, including any late-payment surcharge. Signature field for legal representative. The local legal representative must sign electronically with a Spanish digital certificate. Branch profits subsequently remitted to head office are subject to the separate 19% non-resident branch tax unless the remittance is physically prevented by regulatory capital requirements. Late filing of Form 200 without prior AEAT assessment gives rise to an extemporaneous filing surcharge of 1% per month up to 15%, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75% per annum). A late return with no tax due attracts a fixed fine of EUR 200 to EUR 6,000. Incorrect or false returns trigger proportional penalties under Articles 191–193 LGT: from 50% to 150% of the under-assessed amount, plus interest and administrative costs.
Box I / Instalment Method Indicate whether the prepayment is calculated on the prior-year taxable base basis (Article 40.2 LIS) or the current-year profit basis for large taxpayers (Article 40.3 LIS). A non-resident PE may use the prior-year basis and must adjust for the company's Spanish-only taxable income; current-year basis may be selected only when the taxpayer has real substance and accounting records. Failure to file or pay instalments triggers late-payment surcharges of 1% per month, maximum 15%, plus late-payment interest; if AEAT requires payment, enforcement surcharges up to 20% may apply and tax refunds may be suspended. False or unfounded reductions are treated as regular late-payment infractions.
Box II / Taxable Base and Extent Enter the relevant taxable base or positive accounting profit for the instalment period, applying the statutory rate percentage and any deductions authorised for instalment prepayments. Ensure the taxable base attributable to the PE excludes non-Spanish activities; if the PE has no permanent establishment in prior periods, a nil or reduced instalment may apply. Failure to file or pay instalments triggers late-payment surcharges of 1% per month, maximum 15%, plus late-payment interest; if AEAT requires payment, enforcement surcharges up to 20% may apply and tax refunds may be suspended. False or unfounded reductions are treated as regular late-payment infractions.
Box III / Deductions and Prepayments Report credits and tax prepayments already satisfied in the current period to calculate the net instalment due. Foreign tax credits and treaty reliefs are not automatically recalculated for instalments; use only those credits duly substantiated for the Spanish PE. Failure to file or pay instalments triggers late-payment surcharges of 1% per month, maximum 15%, plus late-payment interest; if AEAT requires payment, enforcement surcharges up to 20% may apply and tax refunds may be suspended. False or unfounded reductions are treated as regular late-payment infractions.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 10,000,000 of annual net turnover triggers the mandatory preparation of the Local File; a Master File is additionally required when the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue reaches EUR 50,000,000 and the Spanish entity carries out related-party transactions. Related-party transactions below EUR 250,000 may be excluded from detailed documentation in limited cases, but the arm's-length standard always applies to the actual transaction.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not apply offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations, but substantive economic presence is enforced through the anti-abuse provisions in Article 15 LIS and Article 15 of the Spanish General Tax Law. For a surgical laparoscopy tower manufacturing SL, economic substance is demonstrated through owned production facilities, employed technical staff, assumption of warranty and regulatory-compliant risk, control of inventory and pricing decisions, and actual management functions performed in Spain. Transactions with related Latin American distribution entities are recharacterised when the purported substance does not correspond to the activity.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return

Statutory sanction: Criminal Code Article 305: imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of six times the defrauded amount; administrative penalty under LGT Articles 191 and 193: 50% to 150% of the under-declared tax, plus late-payment interest and loss of tax benefits.

Director personal liability: Directors face joint and several liability for the corporate tax debt under LGT Article 42.2 when they participated negligently in the fraud. Personal civil liability for damages, attachment of bank accounts and personal assets, travel bans and disqualification from benefiting from public aid may be imposed; the corporate veil is pierced when the SL is used as an instrument of concealment.
Shell Company / Artificial Absence of Substance

Statutory sanction: Recharacterisation of income under Article 15 LIS, denial of treaty benefits, retroactive assessment with interest, and penalties for serious infractions under LGT Article 206 including up to 150% of the deficiency and possible cancellation of the NIF registration.

Director personal liability: Directors who sign backdated minutes, artificial contracts or false declarations may be convicted of false accounting under Criminal Code Article 290; civil liability extends to unpaid corporate tax and social security debt. The court may order disqualification from holding corporate office for up to 15 years and impose travel restrictions where there is a flight risk.
Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Documentation Default

Statutory sanction: AEAT may make an upward transfer pricing adjustment, collect the primary tax liability, apply interest from the original due date, and impose a 15% penalty under Article 18.12 LIS for documentation failure or inaccurate data; where concealment exists, the penalty may reach 150% of the adjustment.

Director personal liability: Directors who approve or sign intercompany pricing arrangements without economic analysis face solidary liability for the resulting corporate tax deficiency when their participation is deemed negligent. In severe cases, insolvency-based liability under Ley Concursal and criminal liability for scheme abuse may be pursued; international tax-exposed directors are subject to asset-tracing and travel bans.
Anti-Money Laundering / Corruption in Export Medical Equipment Sales

Statutory sanction: Administrative sanctions under Law 10/2010 for very serious infractions range from EUR 60,001 to EUR 1,500,000, plus confiscation. Criminal conviction for money laundering under Criminal Code Article 301 leads to imprisonment of 6 months to 6 years, fines, and forfeiture of the SL's assets; foreign officials bribery raises penalties under Article 445 bis.

Director personal liability: Directors and beneficial owners are exposed to personal criminal proceedings, provisional detention, extradition and travel bans when the Spanish SL is integrated into a transnational corruption scheme. Civil liability includes restitution of laundered proceeds, and courts frequently pierce the corporate veil to satisfy confiscation and compensation orders against the personal assets of the directors.
